overview.text: The Kazan icon is especially venerated in the Russian Church, with important examples associated with Kazan, Saint Petersburg and Moscow. The OCA’s July 8 account relates its discovery and the subsequent veneration of multiple copies.

blocks.text: The pictured panel is a mid-nineteenth-century Kazan icon, with smaller saints on the borders. Mary inclines her head beside the upright Christ child. This later example is identified separately from the icon whose discovery is narrated for 1579.

blocks.text: The published Church account places the discovery after a destructive fire in Kazan in 1579. Nine-year-old Matrona reported repeated visions indicating the location. The account names the priest Ermogenes, later patriarch, as a witness who wrote about the finding.

blocks.text: The OCA relates healings of blind people during the icon’s first procession and explains the prominence of its veneration. These reported miracles belong to the source’s Church narrative. The many later copies should not all be called the same original physical object.
